title: TECT-ALT-001 bounded same-condition alternative intake
question: Can a separately defined candidate improve a named exchange criterion under the same charge/time/coefficient conditions without modifying EXCH001?
method: Hash-pin two candidate slots and cheap-first transfer/symmetry/state-cost tests.
Reject density-only coupling at the transfer filter before phase calculations.
Use six Frobenius-orthonormal symmetric tensor coordinates, exact Poisson and covariance controls, and a same-Q same-P1-energy initial response comparison.
Separate structural advantage from all-time response, stability and physical superiority; preserve all state coordinates and stop the bounded intake.
finding: Tensor coupling removes instantaneous internal pair-source cancellation: at the same zero-reservoir state both first charge derivatives vanish, but tensor second response is1849/2916 versus scalar0. This costs six complex reservoir coordinates and does not establish superior stability or physics. Density coupling cannot transfer the component norm charge. Overall superiority remains unestablished.
decision_reason: A verified structural lead is retained as auxiliary_support, not an adopted better physical model or baseline repair.
boundary: No full P1 U3 symmetry, invariant scalar dark sector, all-time transfer dominance, unique state selection, physical time, PreA, QFT, gravity or limit. No third candidate or parameter sweep.
next_action: A separately admitted matched-state actual stability comparison is required before overall ranking; no automatic successor or repeated cancellation test.
